reviewed_scope: recv.rs poll_data / poll_trailers / schedule_recv / is_end_stream / recv_reset / received DATA END_STREAM transition
share.rs RecvStream data / trailers / is_end_stream delegation
streams.rs OpaqueStreamRef polling and reset delegation
client.rs inspect_headers / receive_body and its exchange original-deadline wrapper

findings.conclusion: For an active response receive half without a prior received EOS, recv_reset records Cause::Error(remote_reset). NO_ERROR does not receive a success exemption. ensure_recv_open yields Err, which propagates through schedule_recv when the receive queue is empty.

Buffered DATA is returned before state scheduling. A reset may therefore be observed after some successful DATA items. The candidate checks every item and continues through None; returning any earlier body prefix is not classified as complete.
poll_data returns None when a trailer event is at the front without consuming that event. The candidate separately awaits trailers and rejects trailer errors. No data(None)-only EOS claim is made.
RecvStream.is_end_stream reaches Recv::is_end_stream, requiring both the state to record a received EOS and an empty pending receive queue. It is stronger than an empty body buffer or data(None).

The reset handler preserves previously received EOS as ErrorAfterEndStream, or leaves an already closed unqueued state unchanged. This preservation is not restricted to NO_ERROR. It permits completion of the already received message while retaining a reset for the send side.

The candidate requires a single bounded syntactically strict Content-Length, every DATA item Ok, cumulative bytes within that length, data(None), trailers Ok and empty, actual is_end_stream=true, and final byte count exactly equal to Content-Length before setting response_complete.

The receive operation is under the same until passed to timeout_at. The connection driver is then aborted and awaited under that same deadline; runtime completion and output publication have later deadline checks. This review does not qualify the entire caller, filesystem output, controller, TLS implementation or runtime execution.

limitations: This is a static review of the exact library and candidate source, not a Rust build, real HTTP/2 exchange, packet trace or product/official-CLI qualification.

The EOS conjunction establishes completed receive-message framing plus exact length. It must not be described as proof that no late reset occurred, that a late reset reason was NO_ERROR, or that both halves of the entire connection succeeded.
No h2 error is converted to success merely because its reason is NO_ERROR. Pre-EOS errors still prevent response_complete.
Only the listed candidate methods and surrounding deadline use were reviewed; Spec/input schema, private-output authority and full controller remain under their own review.
